purpose: Preceptor audit: dimension-four interval classification and curvature-functional budget for near-pinched A1 resolutions.

c<0<C.status: cannot be a successful Yau-26 interval in dimension 4
c<0<C.reason: Rescaling any metric makes Ricci eigenvalues arbitrarily close to 0; S1xS3 is closed, connected, smooth, and has no Einstein metric.

c=0<C.reason: S1xS3 with flat x round product has Ric>=0; after constant rescaling Ric<=C g. It has no Einstein metric.

c<0=C.reason: Lohkamp gives a Ric<0 metric on every closed 4-manifold; after constant rescaling it satisfies c g <= Ric <= 0. Use S1xS3, which has no Einstein metric.

0<c<C.status: equivalent to normalized positive branch P_4^+(delta)
0<c<C.delta_formula: delta=(C-c)/(C+c) in (0,1), after scaling by alpha=(C+c)/2

c<C<0.status: equivalent to normalized negative branch P_4^-(delta)
c<C<0.delta_formula: delta=(C-c)/(-(C+c)) in (0,1), after scaling by alpha=-(C+c)/2

S1xS3_no_einstein_certificate.ric_nonnegative_input: flat S1 times unit round S3 has Ricci eigenvalues (0,2,2,2); scaling makes them lie in [0,C] for any C>0.
S1xS3_no_einstein_certificate.ric_nonpositive_input: Lohkamp: every closed n>=3 manifold has a strictly negative Ricci metric; scaling makes it lie in [c,0] for any c<0.
S1xS3_no_einstein_certificate.no_einstein_argument: For an Einstein 4-metric, 8π²χ=∫(|W|²+s²/24). If χ=0, W=0 and s=0; with E=0 this is flat. A closed flat 4-manifold has Bieberbach fundamental group virtually Z^4, unlike Z.

mirror_energy_budgets.label: positive mirror (S2xS2)/Z2
mirror_energy_budgets.interpretation: Near-pinched metrics make E=Ric-(s/4)g tend to 0 in L2 at bounded volume, so F=∫(|W|^2+s^2/24)=8π^2χ+(1/2)∫|E|^2 tends to this closed lower bound.

mirror_energy_budgets.label: negative mirror (Sigma2xSigma2)/<iota x iota>
mirror_energy_budgets.interpretation: Near-pinched metrics make E=Ric-(s/4)g tend to 0 in L2 at bounded volume, so F=∫(|W|^2+s^2/24)=8π^2χ+(1/2)∫|E|^2 tends to this closed lower bound.

variational_identity_4d.attainment: In dimension 4, F attains its lower bound 8π²χ iff E=0, hence (by contracted Bianchi for n>=3) g is Einstein.
variational_identity_4d.near_pinched_consequence: The audited A1 families have bounded volume and ||Ric-sigma g||_op -> 0, so ∫|E|² -> 0 and inf F=8π²χ on every fixed filling pattern covered by the construction.
variational_identity_4d.research_use: The mixed-row Einstein question is an attainment/non-attainment problem for a scale-invariant curvature functional with no energy gap; this explains why purely integral lower bounds leave slack.

full_dimension_four_refutation_requireme.strict_positive_intervals: would be defeated by a no-Einstein-of-any-sign theorem on one positive-mirror mixed row with audited near-positive pinching
full_dimension_four_refutation_requireme.strict_negative_intervals: would be defeated by a no-Einstein-of-any-sign theorem on one negative-mirror mixed row with audited near-negative pinching
full_dimension_four_refutation_requireme.current_status: neither all-sign no-Einstein theorem is known; Yau-26 in dimension 4 remains unresolved
